subject: Post-demo: procurement timeline, PO vs card, and mutual action plan
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@acme-retail.com>, Tom Rourke <tom.rourke@acme-retail.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: procurement timeline, PO vs card, and mutual action plan

Hi Claire / Tom —

Great to meet this morning — thanks for the time and the thoughtful questions. Per request during the call, I pulled together the current procurement milestones we typically see for customers in retail (legal -> security -> finance -> PO issuance) and the practical cadence we recommend to keep the deal on track. I attached a one-page mutual action plan ("Redwood-MAP-v1.pdf") and our short SLA/cost summary.

Quick recap and asks:
- Legal review: usually 7–14 business days for our standard MSA; redlines add time. Can you confirm whether Acme will use an internal MSA or prefer Redwood's standard?
- Security review: we provide SOC2, pen-test summary, and a runbook; security intake normally takes 5–10 business days. Who on your team owns security evidence requests?
- Finance / procurement: PO vs corporate card decision — which is preferred for initial POC? Finance approvals typically need a requester + budget code; if PO, expect 3–7 business days after approvals.
- Marketplace path: you mentioned interest in listing via your internal marketplace—is that still applicable or would you prefer us to proceed direct?

Proposed milestones (high level):
1) Week 0: Sign mutual action plan + confirm approach (PO vs card + marketplace).
2) Week 1–2: Legal & security intake in parallel (we'll create a shared folder for evidence).
3) Week 2–3: Finance approval + PO issuance / card onboarding.
4) Week 3+: Provision dedicated sandbox or start hosted trial.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Claire: confirm security owner and whether Acme will redline our MSA (simple yes/no and name).
2) Tom: confirm preferred commercial instrument (PO or card) for the POC and target date for budget approval.
3) Karthik / Laura: I’ll loop you in for a short intake call with your teams if needed.

Attachments: 2026-03-22-Redwood-MAP-v1.pdf (MAP), redwood-svc-sla-summary.pdf (1-pager).

Thanks — I can be flexible on timing for the procurement check-in; if you can aim for updates by Friday next week (Mar 27) that would be great.

Best,
Ben Carter
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwoodinference.com
+1 415-555-0147

From: Claire Hsu <claire.hsu@acme-retail.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Tom Rourke <tom.rourke@acme-retail.com>
Date: 2026-03-22T14:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-demo: procurement timeline, PO vs card, and mutual action plan

Thanks Ben — useful recap.

Quick answers:
- Legal: Acme will start with Redwood's standard MSA. We already have a legal counsel assigned (Sanjay Patel). He typically does a light pass; if there are large redlines we'll flag them.
- Security: Security owner is me for first pass; I'll pass audit items to our infosec team (cc'd Tom). Please send the SOC2 + pen test artifacts to our shared folder.
- Finance: For the POC we prefer to use a corporate card to avoid the PO lead time, but Procurement would prefer PO for anything > $25k. The initial POC spend should be below that threshold.
- Marketplace: We are curious about a marketplace listing but not required for POC. Let's keep it as a possible later step.

Timeline: we can commit to finishing our internal legal and security intake checks within 7–10 business days provided the artifacts are clear. Finance will confirm card provisioning by 3/26.

Thanks — Claire
Claire Hsu
Sr. PM, Digital Commerce | Acme Retail
claire.hsu@acme-retail.com

Claire — great, thanks for the clarity. A couple operational notes so your team has what it needs: 

- I'll upload SOC2 attestation and the pen-test summary to the Drive folder and share the link (attached in HubSpot and in related_links).
- Because finance prefers a card for POC, we'll provision a trial billing profile that accepts card; when/if you move to production we can switch to PO or marketplace flow.
- Karthik: can you confirm we can accept a card-first POC and still provision any contractual guardrails Acme needs (SLA addendum, data handling addendum)?

Proposed quick checkpoints:
- Thu 3/26: Claire confirms card provisioning status (finance).
- Fri 3/27: Sanjay (Acme legal) to do initial MSA read and flag any non-standard items.
- Wed 4/1: Follow-up call with Karthik & Security if needed.

If that timeline works I'll mark the MAP with those target dates and share an updated PDF.

Thanks — I'll also set a calendar placeholder for 4/1 and share only if we need it.

Ben

Thanks — quick confirmation from the Redwood side:
- Card-first POC is fine. We'll generate a short intake that documents data residency, retention, and the applicable SLA for the trial environment.
- Legal: using Redwood standard MSA will speed things up. If Sanjay has any non-standard redlines, ask for annotated PDF and we can turn around first-pass comments within 3 business days.
- Security: Claire, if you send the exact list of evidence items required, our security ops will prioritize.
- PO path: if Acme opts for PO later, typical internal processing time to create and approve is 5–7 business days once we have the PO request + budget code and authorized signer.

I attached a short checklist that we use for customers moving from POC -> production (filename: redwood-svc-sla-summary.pdf).
